answer.rationale: Finance's 18% cut mandate can't be met by renewal since the incumbent has already refused to reopen price this cycle, and negotiate_terms is effectively foreclosed for this cycle. memory_c2 is the strongest lead for meeting the cost target via a low-cost primary vendor, but it's a single archived data point about past performance (onboarding speed, invoicing accuracy) that predates the current 14-day window and 94%-capacity, no-buffer line condition — a mismatch that materially raises delivery-risk stakes if the claim doesn't hold up. I'm spending the verification budget on memory_c2 to check the original record for caveats (e.g., ramp time, qualification lead time, quality issues) before committing capacity to a switch. Given the tight timeline and zero volume buffer, I'm not proposing a full primary-vendor swap outright; I'm scoping this cycle's action as a guarded, limited cutover (partial volume or expedited dual-track qualification) rather than a broad rollout, preserving the option to fall back to the incumbent on a short extension if the new vendor underperforms. Second-sourcing (c3) and deferral (c5) are reasonable alternatives but don't address the immediate cost mandate or the imminent contract expiration, and this review only affords one decision.
